findings.source_passage: there were other dogs. There could not but be other dogs on so vast a place, but they did not count. They came and went, resided in the populous kennels, or lived obscurely
findings.source_locator: paragraph 3, opening of Buck's domain description
findings.why_it_matters: The rhetorical rhythm of 'There could not but be other dogs on so vast a place, but they did not count' is a voice-establishing aside that carries ironic aristocratic disdain; the draft collapses this to a bare list without the dismissive logic.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the 'they did not count' clause with its explanatory framing to preserve the narrator's ironic register.

findings.source_passage: He had learned the lesson, and in all his after life he never forgot it.
findings.source_locator: paragraph after the club-beating, 'He was beaten (he knew that)' passage
findings.why_it_matters: This sentence is a narratorial summary of interpretive weight—it marks the permanent cognitive imprint of the primitive law and is frequently cited in critical readings of the novel's education/initiation theme; its absence removes the explicit forward-pointing narrative statement.
findings.suggested_fix: Reinsert the sentence verbatim after 'He saw, once for all, that he stood no chance against a man with a club.'

findings.source_passage: he had saved himself by not becoming a mere pampered house-dog. Hunting and kindred outdoor delights had kept down the fat and hardened his muscles; and to him, as to the cold-tubbing races, the love of water had been a tonic and a health preserver.
findings.why_it_matters: The phrase 'kept down the fat' is specific and vivid; more importantly, 'to him, as to the cold-tubbing races' is a distinctive socio-cultural register marker that situates Buck in a Victorian class idiom; reducing it to 'hardened his muscles; to him, as to the cold-tubbing races, the love of water was a tonic' drops 'kept down the fat' and 'a health preserver,' thinning the voice.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'kept down the fat' and 'health preserver' alongside 'tonic' to maintain the full phrase.

findings.source_passage: Perrault was a French-Canadian, and swarthy; but François was a French-Canadian half-breed, and twice as swarthy. They were a new kind of men to Buck (of which he was destined to see many more)
findings.source_locator: paragraph introducing François and Perrault aboard the Narwhal
findings.why_it_matters: The parenthetical 'of which he was destined to see many more' is a narrator-level proleptic aside that shapes the reader's sense of Buck's widening world; its omission slightly reduces narrative voice.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the parenthetical aside '(of which he was destined to see many more)' after 'They were a new kind of men to Buck.'

findings.source_passage: For two days and nights Buck neither ate nor drank... He did not mind the hunger so much, but the lack of water caused him severe suffering
findings.why_it_matters: The distinction 'He did not mind the hunger so much, but the lack of water caused him severe suffering' is a specific psychological observation that characterizes Buck's endurance; the draft omits it, losing a nuance of character.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the 'did not mind the hunger so much' contrast before the water-suffering sentence.

summary: The draft is largely faithful with no high-severity signature losses; three medium findings involve voice-flattening and one missing narratorial summary sentence of interpretive weight, plus two low-severity omissions, but no single finding rises to regeneration-triggering severity and the medium count is below the threshold of three required to force regeneration.
